title: Fall Back! Daylight Saving Time Ends on November 1
summary:
Good news! On Sunday, November 1, 2026, millions of people in North America will get a bonus hour. Clocks go back by one hour. This ends Daylight Saving Time (DST) for this year and gives the weekend an extra 60 minutes.

The change also brings more sunlight into the morning. That should make it a little easier to wake up for school or work during the shorter winter days. This year, DST began on March 8.

Why do we change the clocks at all? The idea started during World War I. In 1916, the German Empire moved clocks forward to save fuel, and the United States and Britain copied the idea. Later, the rules became messy. By 1965, one state, Iowa, had 23 different sets of dates! A 1966 law, the Uniform Time Act, set one schedule for the whole country.

Since 2007, DST has run from the second Sunday in March to the first Sunday in November. About 70 countries use some form of it. So remember: fall back, and enjoy the extra hour!
why_it_matters: The clock change gives you an extra hour in your weekend, and brighter mornings can make waking up for school a little easier.

keywords.explanation: The practice of moving clocks forward in spring and back in autumn so the day has more light in the evening.
A large group of countries or lands all ruled by one leader, such as an emperor.
A United States law that gave the whole country one shared schedule for changing the clocks.
Something extra that you get on top of what you normally have.

questions.question: What will happen to the clocks on November 1?
options: They will go back by one hour
They will stop for one hour
They will go forward by one hour
They will not change at all
questions.correct_answer: They will go back by one hour

questions.question: What extra thing do people get when the clocks go back?
options: A shorter school week
An extra day of holiday
A later sunset
A bonus hour

questions.question: Why did the German Empire first move its clocks forward in 1916?
options: To start a new calendar
To save fuel
To confuse other countries
To make mornings darker

questions.question: What was the problem in Iowa by 1965?
options: It refused to change its clocks
It changed its clocks every week
It had no clocks at all
It had 23 different sets of clock-change dates
questions.correct_answer: It had 23 different sets of clock-change dates

questions.question: What did the Uniform Time Act of 1966 do?
options: It moved the clocks by two hours
It set one schedule for the whole country
It gave every state its own dates
It ended Daylight Saving Time forever
questions.correct_answer: It set one schedule for the whole country

questions.question: Since 2007, when does Daylight Saving Time end each year?
options: On the second Sunday in March
On the first Sunday in November
On the last Sunday in October
On the first day of winter
questions.correct_answer: On the first Sunday in November

background_read: Daylight Saving Time is a system where everyone moves their clocks forward in spring and back again in autumn. Moving the clocks changes which hours are light, giving people longer light evenings in summer and brighter mornings in winter. The idea began as a way to save fuel, and a law later gave the whole country one schedule so the clock-change dates would be the same everywhere.
Article_Structure: WHO: Millions of people in North America who use Daylight Saving Time
WHAT: Clocks go back by one hour, ending Daylight Saving Time for the year and adding a bonus hour to the weekend
WHERE: Across North America, including the United States
WHY: The change brings more sunlight into winter mornings, and the system grew from a fuel-saving idea that later needed one shared national schedule
